scope: Read-only adversarial review of all 12 full ballot objects in ballots.review.json (jet-refounding-20260905)
findings: ballots.review.json:D-ENDPOINT-SHAPE1.recommendation.whyNot[1]: 🟡 risk: Option C's stated gain "Protocol can be authored before implementation" (options[2].gains[0]) is never rebutted — whyNot[C] only restates the mechanism ("A separate protocol declaration remains"), which is also true of A's handler-as-descriptor before it exists, so it does not defeat C's contract-first workflow value. Fix: give whyNot[C] a real cost (e.g. protocol/handler can diverge pre-binding, or two artifacts must stay synchronized across teams) or scope rec:A to single-team/same-repo cases and concede C for contract-first orgs.

ballots.review.json:D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1.options[0].code vs recommendation.why: 🔴 bug: recommendation.why claims A avoids "requiring generic notation at every ordinary call," but the worked proposed line is `mouse :: Point2<Float, Screen>.new(240.0, 120.0)` — raw generic notation, not a stock alias/constructor as detail promises ("Stock constructors and aliases are real domain names"). The example contradicts the recommendation's own ergonomic claim. Fix: show the promised stock-alias call (e.g. `Screen.point(240.0, 120.0)`) in the worked example, or drop the ergonomic claim from recommendation.why.

ballots.review.json:D-MODEL-BACKEND1.detail ("ONNX Runtime v1.29.0, published 2026-08-12"): ❓ question: version+date pin has no embedded citation URL or captured evidence artifact — unlike sibling D-DATA-READER1.inWild, which embeds the exact pinned version directly in its docs.rs URL. This ballot's inWild only links a generic unversioned doc page (onnxruntime.ai/docs/api/python/api_summary.html); repo search finds no evidence file backing '1.29.0'/'2026-08-12' anywhere under docs/audits. Fix: cite the exact GitHub release/tag URL sourcing the version and date, matching the evidentiary bar the parquet ballot already meets.

ballots.review.json:D-DATA-READER1.detail ("F07a remains a separate ABI-only choice"): 🟡 risk: 'F07a' is used to draw a scope boundary against D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1 but is not a registered label anywhere else in the corpus — grep of docs/audits/jet-refounding-2026-09-05 finds zero other 'F07a' occurrences; only 'F07' (index.md, 03-tools-and-systems.md) is defined, and it already bundles both ABI sharing and file-query framing. An invented, unregistered sub-label is doing scope-boundary work. Fix: define F07a explicitly in index.md's feature table (or rename the reference to the registered F07) so the split is checkable.

ballots.review.json:D-TEST-HISTORY1.detail ("The model cannot call production logic for the behavior being checked"): 🟡 risk: this is a soundness precondition for the entire differential-testing design — a model that transitively calls production would trivially agree with it, defeating the oracle. None of the 4 acceptance bullets or checkInstructions verify model independence; bullet 3 only requires recording discard/bounds data, not checking the model has no dependency edge into the module under test. Fix: add an acceptance criterion enforcing model/production separation (module-graph check or explicit no-call assertion), not prose intent alone.

ballots.review.json:D-QUERY-RETAIN1.detail (worked contract) vs checkInstructions[1]: 🟡 risk: the only worked contract given ("two Core tickets of 4.0 and 8.0 minutes produce Group{key: Core, value: 6.0} for mean") demonstrates the trivial case — Float mean of Float inputs, which stays Float with no risk of misbehavior. It never demonstrates the actual at-risk acceptance claim, checkInstructions[1]/options[0].technical: "Nominal keys and exact integer/unit sums do not become String or Float merely to satisfy aggregation." Fix: add a worked contract for `.sum()` over Int- or unit-typed input showing the result type stays exactly Int/unit, since that's the case where silent Float promotion would actually surface.
